claim: Placental malaria (PM) is most frequent and severe in first pregnancies.
source: Placental malaria (PM) is a deadly syndrome most frequent and severe in first pregnancies.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract without supporting data in the manuscript, but is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: PM results from accumulation of Plasmodium falciparum-infected erythrocytes (IE) that express the surface antigen VAR2CSA and bind to chondroitin sulfate A (CSA) in the placenta.
source: PM results from accumulation of Plasmodium falciparum-infected erythrocytes (IE) that express the surface antigen VAR2CSA and bind to chondroitin sulfate A (CSA) in the placenta.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction (Fried and Duffy, 1996; Salanti et al., 2003; Tuikue Ndam et al., 2005) and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Women become PM-resistant over successive pregnancies as they develop anti-adhesion and anti-VAR2CSA antibodies.
source: Women become PM-resistant over successive pregnancies as they develop anti-adhesion and anti-VAR2CSA antibodies, supporting VAR2CSA as the leading PM-vaccine candidate.
evidence: This is supported by citations in the introduction (Fried and Duffy, 1998; Ricke et al., 2000; Salanti et al., 2004; Ndam et al., 2015) and represents established knowledge.

claim: The first VAR2CSA subunit vaccines failed to induce broadly neutralizing antibody.
source: However, the first VAR2CSA subunit vaccines failed to induce broadly neutralizing antibody and it is known that naturally acquired antibodies target both variant-specific and conserved epitopes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical trials (Mordmüller et al., 2019; Sirima et al., 2020) mentioned in the introduction.

claim: Naturally acquired antibodies target both variant-specific and conserved epitopes.
source: However, the first VAR2CSA subunit vaccines failed to induce broadly neutralizing antibody and it is known that naturally acquired antibodies target both variant-specific and conserved epitopes.
evidence: This represents established knowledge in the field, supported by the discussion of naturally acquired immunity.

claim: The five VAR2CSA variants purified ~0.7% of total IgG.
source: The five VAR2CSA variants purified ~0.7% of total IgG and yielded both strain-transcending and strain-specific reactivity to VAR2CSA and IE-surface antigen.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1, where 386.1 µg was purified from 58,000 µg total IgG.

claim: The five VAR2CSA variants yielded both strain-transcending and strain-specific reactivity to VAR2CSA and IE-surface antigen.
source: The five VAR2CSA variants purified ~0.7% of total IgG and yielded both strain-transcending and strain-specific reactivity to VAR2CSA and IE-surface antigen.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2 and 3, demonstrating reactivity patterns.

claim: IgG purified on the first VAR2CSA antigen displayed broad cross-reactivity to both recombinant and native VAR2CSA variants.
source: In two independent antibody purification/depletion experiments with permutated order of VAR2CSA variants, IgG purified on the first VAR2CSA antigen displayed broad cross-reactivity to both recombinant and native VAR2CSA variants, and inhibited binding of all isolates to CSA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 3, 4, and 5 showing cross-reactivity and inhibition patterns.

claim: IgG purified on the first VAR2CSA antigen inhibited binding of all isolates to CSA.
source: In two independent antibody purification/depletion experiments with permutated order of VAR2CSA variants, IgG purified on the first VAR2CSA antigen displayed broad cross-reactivity to both recombinant and native VAR2CSA variants, and inhibited binding of all isolates to CSA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 4 and 5 showing CSA-binding inhibition activity.

claim: IgG remaining after depletion on all variants showed significantly reduced binding-inhibition activity compared to initial total IgG.
source: IgG remaining after depletion on all variants showed significantly reduced binding-inhibition activity compared to initial total IgG.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 2C showing reduced inhibition activity after depletion.

claim: A single VAR2CSA ectodomain variant displays conserved epitopes that are targeted by neutralizing antibodies shared by multiple parasite strains, including maternal isolates.
source: These findings demonstrate that a single VAR2CSA ectodomain variant displays conserved epitopes that are targeted by neutralizing (or binding-inhibitory) antibodies shared by multiple parasite strains, including maternal isolates.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental data showing that IgG purified on a single variant can inhibit multiple isolates.

claim: A broadly effective PM-vaccine can be achieved with a limited number of VAR2CSA variants.
source: This suggests that a broadly effective PM-vaccine can be achieved with a limited number of VAR2CSA variants.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings that a single variant can purify broadly neutralizing antibodies.

claim: PM has been linked to several adverse pregnancy outcomes.
source: PM has been linked to several adverse pregnancy outcomes (Steketee et al., 2001; Guyatt and Snow, 2001; Desai et al., 2007; Moore et al., 2017), and first-time mothers are most vulnerable (Brabin, 1983).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: First-time mothers are most vulnerable to PM.
source: PM has been linked to several adverse pregnancy outcomes (Steketee et al., 2001; Guyatt and Snow, 2001; Desai et al., 2007; Moore et al., 2017), and first-time mothers are most vulnerable (Brabin, 1983).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Brabin, 1983.

claim: Over successive pregnancies, PM and the related sequalae become less prevalent.
source: Over successive pregnancies, PM and the related sequalae become less prevalent (Guyatt and Snow, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Guyatt and Snow, 2001.

claim: Susceptibility to PM has been attributed to P. falciparum parasites that bind chondroitin sulphate-A (CSA) expressed by the placental syncytiotrophoblast.
source: Susceptibility to PM has been attributed to P. falciparum parasites that bind chondroitin sulphate-A (CSA) expressed by the placental syncytiotrophoblast (Fried and Duffy, 1996), and express the variant surface antigen VAR2CSA (Salanti et al., 2003; Tuikue Ndam et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fried and Duffy, 1996.

claim: PM-susceptible parasites express the variant surface antigen VAR2CSA.
source: Susceptibility to PM has been attributed to P. falciparum parasites that bind chondroitin sulphate-A (CSA) expressed by the placental syncytiotrophoblast (Fried and Duffy, 1996), and express the variant surface antigen VAR2CSA (Salanti et al., 2003; Tuikue Ndam et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Salanti et al., 2003 and Tuikue Ndam et al., 2005.

claim: The decrease in PM-related poor pregnancy outcomes with increasing parity is associated with the acquisition of functional antibodies to CSA-binding IE.
source: Conversely, the decrease in PM-related poor pregnancy outcomes with increasing parity is associated with the acquisition of functional antibodies to CSA-binding IE (Fried and Duffy, 1998; Ricke et al., 2000) and antibodies to VAR2CSA (Salanti et al., 2004; Ndam et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fried and Duffy, 1998 and Ricke et al., 2000.

claim: The decrease in PM-related poor pregnancy outcomes with increasing parity is associated with antibodies to VAR2CSA.
source: Conversely, the decrease in PM-related poor pregnancy outcomes with increasing parity is associated with the acquisition of functional antibodies to CSA-binding IE (Fried and Duffy, 1998; Ricke et al., 2000) and antibodies to VAR2CSA (Salanti et al., 2004; Ndam et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Salanti et al., 2004 and Ndam et al., 2015.

claim: Functional antibodies have been characterized for two major functions: blocking CSA-binding of VAR2CSA-expressing parasites and opsonizing IE to promote phagocytosis.
source: Such functional antibodies have been characterized for two major functions: (1) blocking CSA-binding of VAR2CSA-expressing parasites and (2) opsonizing IE to promote phagocytosis (Fried and Duffy, 1998; Ricke et al., 2000; Duffy and Fried, 2003; Keen et al., 2007; Ataíde et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: VAR2CSA represents the leading candidate for PM vaccine development.
source: Hence, VAR2CSA represents the leading candidate for PM vaccine development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the established knowledge about VAR2CSA's role in PM and naturally acquired immunity.

claim: VAR2CSA is a large (∼318–478 kDa) multidomain transmembrane protein.
source: VAR2CSA is a large (∼318–478 kDa) multidomain transmembrane protein, a member of the P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 (PfEMP1) family encoded by var genes (Gardner et al., 2002; Hviid and Jensen, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gardner et al., 2002 and Hviid and Jensen, 2015.

claim: VAR2CSA is a member of the P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 (PfEMP1) family encoded by var genes.
source: VAR2CSA is a large (∼318–478 kDa) multidomain transmembrane protein, a member of the P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 (PfEMP1) family encoded by var genes (Gardner et al., 2002; Hviid and Jensen, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gardner et al., 2002 and Hviid and Jensen, 2015.

claim: The cysteine-rich ectodomain is formed by N-terminal sequence (NTS), six and sometimes more Duffy-binding-like (DBL) domains as well as interdomain (ID) regions.
source: The cysteine-rich ectodomain is formed by N-terminal sequence (NTS), six and sometimes more Duffy-binding-like (DBL) domains as well as interdomain (ID) regions (Kraemer and Smith, 2006; Doritchamou et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kraemer and Smith, 2006 and Doritchamou et al., 2019.

claim: VAR2CSA ectodomain structure includes a stable core (NTS-DBL1X-ID1-DBL2X-ID2-DBL3X-DBL4e-ID3) flanked by a flexible arm (DBL5e -DBL6e).
source: Recent studies showed that VAR2CSA ectodomain structure includes a stable core (NTS-DBL1X-ID1-DBL2X-ID2-DBL3X-DBL4e-ID3) flanked by a flexible arm (DBL5e -DBL6e), and the receptor interaction involves CSA threading through two channels that formed within the stable core (Ma et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ma et al., 2021 and Wang et al., 2021.

claim: The receptor interaction involves CSA threading through two channels that formed within the stable core.
source: Recent studies showed that VAR2CSA ectodomain structure includes a stable core (NTS-DBL1X-ID1-DBL2X-ID2-DBL3X-DBL4e-ID3) flanked by a flexible arm (DBL5e -DBL6e), and the receptor interaction involves CSA threading through two channels that formed within the stable core (Ma et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ma et al., 2021 and Wang et al., 2021.

claim: Multiple individual DBL domains of VAR2CSA interact with CSA in vitro.
source: Multiple individual DBL domains of VAR2CSA interact with CSA in vitro (Dahlbäck et al., 2011; Clausen et al., 2012; Ma et al., 2021) and induce functional antibodies in animals (Bigey et al., 2011; Fried et al., 2013; Nielsen and Salanti, 2015; Chêne et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dahlbäck et al., 2011, Clausen et al., 2012, and Ma et al., 2021.

claim: Individual DBL domains induce functional antibodies in animals.
source: Multiple individual DBL domains of VAR2CSA interact with CSA in vitro (Dahlbäck et al., 2011; Clausen et al., 2012; Ma et al., 2021) and induce functional antibodies in animals (Bigey et al., 2011; Fried et al., 2013; Nielsen and Salanti, 2015; Chêne et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bigey et al., 2011, Fried et al., 2013, Nielsen and Salanti, 2015, and Chêne et al., 2018.

claim: Two subunit vaccine candidates (called PAMVAC and PRIMVAC) from the N-terminal region of VAR2CSA were recently tested in phase one trials.
source: Two subunit vaccine candidates (called PAMVAC and PRIMVAC) from the N-terminal region of VAR2CSA were recently tested in phase one trials (Mordmüller et al., 2019; Sirima et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mordmüller et al., 2019 and Sirima et al., 2020.

claim: Both VAR2CSA subunit vaccines were safe, immunogenic and induced functional anti-adhesion antibodies in malaria-naive and malaria-exposed women.
source: Both trial teams reported that VAR2CSA subunit vaccines were safe, immunogenic and induced functional anti-adhesion antibodies in malaria-naive and malaria-exposed women (Mordmüller et al., 2019; Sirima et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mordmüller et al., 2019 and Sirima et al., 2020.

claim: Functional activity of VAR2CSA subunit vaccines was primarily against homologous parasites and low or absent against heterologous parasites.
source: However, functional activity was primarily against homologous parasites (same VAR2CSA sequence as vaccine) and low or absent against heterologous parasites (Sirima et al., 2020), suggesting the vaccine antigen failed to display functional epitopes shared across multiple P. falciparum variants (reviewed in Doritchamou et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sirima et al., 2020.

claim: VAR2CSA fragments fail to purify the broadly neutralizing activity of sera from PM-resistant multigravidae.
source: Similarly, VAR2CSA fragments (single or double domains) fail to purify the broadly neutralizing activity of sera from PM-resistant multigravidae (Doritchamou et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Doritchamou et al., 2016.

claim: VAR2CSA fragments purified antibodies with CSA-binding inhibitory activity against homologous parasites.
source: Although VAR2CSA fragments (including constructs similar to PAMVAC vaccine) purified antibodies with CSA-binding inhibitory activity against homologous parasites, broadly neutralizing activity was neither purified nor depleted after passing sera over several VAR2CSA domains and variants (Doritchamou et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Doritchamou et al., 2016.

claim: Broadly neutralizing activity was neither purified nor depleted after passing sera over several VAR2CSA domains and variants.
source: Although VAR2CSA fragments (including constructs similar to PAMVAC vaccine) purified antibodies with CSA-binding inhibitory activity against homologous parasites, broadly neutralizing activity was neither purified nor depleted after passing sera over several VAR2CSA domains and variants (Doritchamou et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Doritchamou et al., 2016.

claim: The strain-transcending human monoclonal antibody PAM1.4 is specific for an unknown conformational epitope on full-length VAR2CSA.
source: These data supports the hypothesis that functional antibodies to VAR2CSA may target conformational epitopes not displayed by any individual domain: for example, the strain-transcending human monoclonal antibody PAM1.4 is specific for an unknown conformational epitope on full-length VAR2CSA (Barfod et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Barfod et al., 2007.

claim: Naturally acquired antibodies of multiparous women exhibit broadly neutralizing anti-adhesion activity.
source: Naturally acquired antibodies of multiparous women exhibit broadly neutralizing anti-adhesion activity (Fried and Duffy, 1998; Ricke et al., 2000; Ndam et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fried and Duffy, 1998, Ricke et al., 2000, and Ndam et al., 2015.

claim: The affinity purification of IgG specific to five VAR2CSA ectodomain variants yielded a combined ~386.1 µg of VAR2CSA-specific IgG, representing about 0.7% of the original total IgG.
source: The affinity purification of IgG specific to five VAR2CSA ectodomain variants yielded a combined ~386.1 µg of VAR2CSA-specific IgG, representing about 0.7% of the original total IgG (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1.

claim: The highest yields of purified IgG were obtained on the first two variants (NF54 and 7G8) totaling 76% of the IgG purified on all five variants.
source: The highest yields of purified IgG were obtained on the first two variants (NF54 and 7G8) totaling 76% of the IgG purified on all five variants.
evidence: This is calculated from the data in Table 1 showing 145.6 µg and 148.9 µg for NF54 and 7G8 respectively.

claim: IgG reactivity to NF54, 7G8, FCR3, HB3, and M. Camp variants were successfully depleted from the total IgG pool.
source: As expected, IgG reactivity to NF54, 7G8, FCR3, HB3, and M. Camp variants were successfully depleted from the total IgG pool, as demonstrated by the absence of reactivity in each post-depletion sample (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Substantially reduced reactivity to M920 and M200101 was seen in the post-depletion total IgG, indicating that cross-reactive IgG to these two antigens was also depleted.
source: Of note, substantially reduced reactivity to M920 and M200101 (not used in the affinity purification assay) was seen in the post-depletion total IgG, indicating that cross-reactive IgG to these two antigens was also depleted.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Reactivity to native VAR2CSA measured on the IE surface by flow cytometry was depleted in the post-depletion IgG when tested on NF54, WF12/7G8, FCR3 and Malayan Camp isolates.
source: Similarly, reactivity to native VAR2CSA measured on the IE surface by flow cytometry was depleted in the post-depletion IgG when tested on NF54, WF12/7G8, FCR3 and Malayan Camp (M. Camp) isolates (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: WF12 is a progeny of 7G8 X GB4 and its genome encodes the 7G8 VAR2CSA variant.
source: Of note, WF12 (here named WF12/7G8) is a progeny of 7G8 X GB4 (Hayton et al., 2008) and its genome encodes the 7G8 VAR2CSA variant (Figure 2—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hayton et al., 2008 and sequence analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Reactivity of post-depletion total IgG to native VAR2CSA of heterologous maternal isolates (M2022170, M2001190, and M0736) was substantially reduced versus the pre-depletion total IgG.
source: Further, reactivity of post-depletion total IgG to native VAR2CSA of heterologous maternal isolates (M2022170, M2001190, and M0736) was substantially reduced versus the pre-depletion total IgG.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Depletion of IgG on the five VAR2CSA variants reduced CSA-binding inhibition activity in the total IgG.
source: Importantly, depletion of IgG on the five VAR2CSA variants also reduced CSA-binding inhibition activity in the total IgG, being abolished against some isolates and significantly reduced against others (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The inhibition activity of the original pre-depletion total IgG sample was >65% against all parasite lines including recently adapted maternal isolates, except for FCR3 whose binding was inhibited 33%.
source: The inhibition activity of the original pre-depletion total IgG sample was >65% against all parasite lines including recently adapted maternal isolates, except for FCR3 whose binding was inhibited 33% (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: After the depletion of VAR2CSA-specific IgG, the % reduction in inhibition activity ranged from 45% against M2022170% to 87% against NF54.
source: After the depletion of VAR2CSA-specific IgG, the inhibition activity was substantially reduced, with the % reduction (measured as (pre-depletion % inhibition-post-depletion % inhibition)/(pre-depletion % inhibition) x 100) ranging from 45% against M2022170% to 87% against NF54 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: CSA-binding inhibition activity was substantially reduced against the three maternal isolates, implying that a significant fraction of cross-inhibitory IgG to the maternal isolates were also depleted on the heterologous VAR2CSA antigens.
source: CSA-binding inhibition activity was substantially reduced against the three maternal isolates (including M2022170), implying that a significant fraction of cross-inhibitory IgG to the maternal isolates were also depleted on the heterologous VAR2CSA antigens.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing reduced inhibition activity against maternal isolates after depletion.

claim: VAR2CSA-purified IgG exhibited cross-reactivity in ELISA to different variants including M920 and M200101.
source: VAR2CSA-purified IgG exhibited cross-reactivity in ELISA to different variants including M920 and M200101 (Figure 3A), although the degree of this dropped substantially after the first purification.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The degree of cross-reactivity dropped substantially after the first purification.
source: VAR2CSA-purified IgG exhibited cross-reactivity in ELISA to different variants including M920 and M200101 (Figure 3A), although the degree of this dropped substantially after the first purification.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A showing decreasing OD values for subsequent purifications.

claim: NF54-purified IgG reacted to homologous and heterologous VAR2CSA antigens at the highest level of any IgG.
source: Thus, NF54-purified IgG (NF54-IgG) reacted to homologous and heterologous VAR2CSA antigens at the highest level of any IgG, while IgG purified on M. Camp (the last antigen used in the purification/depletion series) showed no cross-reactivity to NF54, 7G8, FCR3, or HB3 variants.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: IgG purified on M. Camp showed no cross-reactivity to NF54, 7G8, FCR3, or HB3 variants.
source: Thus, NF54-purified IgG (NF54-IgG) reacted to homologous and heterologous VAR2CSA antigens at the highest level of any IgG, while IgG purified on M. Camp (the last antigen used in the purification/depletion series) showed no cross-reactivity to NF54, 7G8, FCR3, or HB3 variants.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Each variant purified specific reactivity to itself, albeit at lower OD values than that seen with the initial NF54 purification.
source: Notably, each variant purified specific reactivity to itself, albeit at lower OD values than that seen with the initial NF54 purification, which may indicate the greater abundance and/or greater affinity of cross-reactive versus variant-specific IgG acquired by multigravidae.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The greater abundance and/or greater affinity of cross-reactive versus variant-specific IgG acquired by multigravidae may be indicated by the higher OD values for NF54 purification.
source: Notably, each variant purified specific reactivity to itself, albeit at lower OD values than that seen with the initial NF54 purification, which may indicate the greater abundance and/or greater affinity of cross-reactive versus variant-specific IgG acquired by multigravidae.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: NF54-IgG showed the greatest breadth of reactivity with detectable reactivity to IE surface of all parasites including the maternal isolates.
source: NF54-IgG showed the greatest breadth of reactivity (defined as the number of isolates recognized) with detectable reactivity to IE surface of all parasites including the maternal isolates (known to be polyclonal parasite samples).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: NF54-IgG displayed the highest level of reactivity to all the isolates.
source: NF54-IgG also displayed the highest level of reactivity to all the isolates (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B with MFI values.

claim: IgG subsequently purified on 7G8, FCR3, and M. Camp ectodomains demonstrated lower surface reactivity to the homologous parasite and lower cross-reactivity to the maternal isolates compared to NF54-IgG.
source: Compared to NF54-IgG, IgG subsequently purified on 7G8, FCR3, and M. Camp ectodomains demonstrated lower surface reactivity to the homologous parasite and lower cross-reactivity to the maternal isolates.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: HB3-IgG displayed weaker cross-reactivity to different heterologous lab strain parasites compared to the other purified IgG.
source: Although the HB3-IgG was not tested against its homologous parasite line, this antigen-specific purified IgG displayed weaker cross-reactivity to different heterologous lab strain parasites compared to the other purified IgG.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Reactivity by flow cytometry was lost against parasite isolates after their corresponding recombinant ectodomain had been used in the series of depletion/purifications.
source: As with ELISA, reactivity by flow cytometry was lost against parasite isolates after their corresponding recombinant ectodomain had been used in the series of depletion/purifications, attesting to the complete depletion of homologous IE-surface reactivity by each homologous antigen.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: NF54-IgG contained the largest fraction of the inhibitory activity, with mean nBIA values > 50% against all isolates and hovering around 100% for most.
source: NF54-IgG contained the largest fraction of the inhibitory activity, with mean nBIA values > 50% against all isolates and hovering around 100% for most (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Three recently adapted heterologous maternal isolates showed both the lowest (M2022170) and highest (M2001190) nBIA levels respectively at 56% and 111% inhibition.
source: This included three recently adapted heterologous maternal isolates, which showed both the lowest (M2022170) and highest (M2001190) nBIA levels respectively at 56% and 111% inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Titration of the inhibitory capacity of NF54-IgG against the homologous parasite indicated that blocking is achieved at IgG concentration as low as 10 µg/mL.
source: Interestingly, titration of the inhibitory capacity of NF54-IgG against the homologous parasite indicated that blocking is achieved at IgG concentration as low as 10 µg/mL (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: 7G8-IgG showed lower levels of nBIA than NF54-IgG against all heterologous isolates, except against the maternal isolate M2022170 where 7G8-igG showed similar levels of nBIA to NF54-IgG.
source: 7G8-IgG showed lower levels of nBIA than NF54-IgG against all heterologous isolates, except against the maternal isolate M2022170 where 7G8-igG showed similar levels of nBIA to NF54-IgG; as expected 7G8-IgG (and subsequent variant-purified IgG) showed essentially no activity against NF54 parasites (Figure 4B–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4B-E.

claim: 7G8-IgG and subsequent variant-purified IgG showed essentially no activity against NF54 parasites.
source: 7G8-IgG showed lower levels of nBIA than NF54-IgG against all heterologous isolates, except against the maternal isolate M2022170 where 7G8-igG showed similar levels of nBIA to NF54-IgG; as expected 7G8-IgG (and subsequent variant-purified IgG) showed essentially no activity against NF54 parasites (Figure 4B–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4B-E.

claim: Subsequent purifications of IgG on ectodomain variants continued to yield some level of homologous activity, as seen with WF12/7G8, FCR3, and M. Camp.
source: Subsequent purifications of IgG on ectodomain variants continued to yield some level of homologous activity, as seen with WF12/7G8, FCR3, and M. Camp (Figure 4C and E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4C and E.

claim: IgG purified on VAR2CSA variants demonstrated homologous inhibition activity while displaying high levels of cross-inhibition activity with initial purifications that generally waned with successive purifications.
source: Taken together, the IgG purified on VAR2CSA variants clearly demonstrated homologous inhibition activity while displaying high levels of cross-inhibition activity with initial purifications that generally waned with successive purifications.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental data shown in Figures 4A-E.

claim: IgG purified on the initial variant (M. Camp) exhibited the highest cross-reactivity to heterologous variants of recombinant VAR2CSA in the second purification/depletion experiment.
source: IgG purified on the initial variant (M. Camp) exhibited the highest cross-reactivity to heterologous variants of recombinant VAR2CSA (Figure 5A) and native antigen expressed by CSA-binding isolates (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: M. Camp-IgG exhibited the highest cross-reactivity to native antigen expressed by CSA-binding isolates in the second purification/depletion experiment.
source: IgG purified on the initial variant (M. Camp) exhibited the highest cross-reactivity to heterologous variants of recombinant VAR2CSA (Figure 5A) and native antigen expressed by CSA-binding isolates (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: M. Camp-IgG strongly cross-inhibited the binding of M. Camp, FCR3 and NF54 parasites to CSA.
source: In the functional assay, M. Camp-IgG strongly cross-inhibited the binding of M. Camp, FCR3 and NF54 parasites to CSA (Figure 5C, D and E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5C, D, and E.

claim: The observation with M. Camp-IgG is consistent with the pattern observed with IgG purified on NF54 variant of VAR2CSA in the first purification/depletion experiment.
source: This observation is consistent with the pattern observed with IgG purified on NF54 variant of VAR2CSA in the first purification/depletion experiment.
evidence: This is an inference comparing results from two independent experiments.

claim: Strain-transcending naturally acquired anti-adhesion antibodies can be purified on a single recombinant VAR2CSA ectodomain.
source: It is therefore likely that larger fragments of VAR2CSA would offer a broader spectrum of functional epitopes including conformational epitopes and those present in other fragments missing from the subunits tested. Supporting this hypothesis, the present data demonstrate that strain-transcending naturally acquired anti-adhesion antibodies can be purified on a single recombinant VAR2CSA ectodomain, providing additional evidence that define VAR2CSA as the major target of functional antibodies.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data from the study.

claim: VAR2CSA is the major target of functional antibodies.
source: It is therefore likely that larger fragments of VAR2CSA would offer a broader spectrum of functional epitopes including conformational epitopes and those present in other fragments missing from the subunits tested. Supporting this hypothesis, the present data demonstrate that strain-transcending naturally acquired anti-adhesion antibodies can be purified on a single recombinant VAR2CSA ectodomain, providing additional evidence that define VAR2CSA as the major target of functional antibodies.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data and previous studies.

claim: Naturally acquired anti-adhesion antibodies in PM target VAR2CSA.
source: This conclusion is well-supported by previous studies showing that naturally acquired anti-adhesion antibodies in PM target VAR2CSA (Bigey et al., 2011; Doritchamou et al., 2016), even though other invariant proteins are highly expressed by placental parasites (Francis et al., 2007; Fried et al., 2007; Tuikue Ndam et al., 2008; Bertin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bigey et al., 2011 and Doritchamou et al., 2016.

claim: Other invariant proteins are highly expressed by placental parasites.
source: This conclusion is well-supported by previous studies showing that naturally acquired anti-adhesion antibodies in PM target VAR2CSA (Bigey et al., 2011; Doritchamou et al., 2016), even though other invariant proteins are highly expressed by placental parasites (Francis et al., 2007; Fried et al., 2007; Tuikue Ndam et al., 2008; Bertin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Francis et al., 2007, Fried et al., 2007, Tuikue Ndam et al., 2008, and Bertin et al., 2013.

claim: Anti-adhesion activity of antibodies targeting invariant proteins has not been reported.
source: Anti-adhesion activity of antibodies targeting these invariant proteins has not been reported thus far, and whether these proteins play a role in parasite binding to CSA is still unclear.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of evidence in the literature.
